scope: Actual py5 0.10.11a0 JAVA2D execution of the editable PathMarks starter through its setup and key_pressed callbacks. Raw retained movement/commands are unchanged; the fixed-canvas starter submits only segments whose complete bbox intersects [-1,641]². This is target-specific edit, retained-movement, command, cached-save, and visual-mechanism validation; it is not upstream pixel reproduction, physical-keyboard testing, clipping, or cross-host pixel identity.

checks: saved RGBA pixels equal the displayed ordinal-7 canvas
no eighth composition during a 300ms quiet observation

native_checks: all seven state records are observed in the actual starter callbacks
each completed frame records separate raw source and submitted visible command counts

before a native attempt, pure Python validates every submitted command for all seven states through the shared drawing normalizer and proves each omitted raw command bbox misses [-1,641]² while retained command order is a raw subsequence
M, M, L, and C retain the identical PathMarks and underlying path objects
N and D replace PathMarks and all 24 underlying paths
count-2001 retains the exact 2000-step point and heading prefix
distance-0.8 preserves heading zero and changes at least one later heading
marks replay has exact displayed RGBA pixels
all three visual artifacts and the saved image are opaque, 640x640, and non-background
the S callback saves the already displayed canvas without composition
visual_acceptance: Root and Sol inspect marks.png, trace.png, and long-marks.png for continuous varying paths, coherent perpendicular marks, and length-driven coverage change. They compare the mechanism with the accepted private CP2 images without claiming raster identity.
failure_policy: The executor reserves one exclusive attempt under .work/processing-render.lock before launch. Any failure, including timeout, consumes that attempt, preserves stdout/stderr/result information, terminates the process group, and permits no automatic retry.
